title: Blended thread for tonal effects
subtitle: Combining a coloured strand with black shifts the apparent tone of a fill
excerpt: A fill stitched with one black strand and one dark grey strand sits visually between a pure black fill and a pure grey fill. Blending strands in the needle is the quick way to extend a single-colour blackwork palette into a range of tones without changing the pattern.
sourceNotes: Therese de Dillmont, Encyclopaedia of Needlework (1886), Project Gutenberg #20776. Observations from needlework tradition; blended needle is a standard technique in counted embroidery.

glossaryTerms.definition: Threading more than one colour of stranded cotton together in a single needle to produce a mixed tone in each stitch.
A divisible embroidery thread made of six loosely twisted strands. Separate the strands and recombine the number you need.

content.text: carries two separate colours or shades in the same needle. Each stitch places both threads simultaneously, producing a mixed tone that reads as a single intermediate value from a viewing distance.

before threading. For a two-strand needle at 28-count, you might combine one strand of DMC 310 (black) with one strand of DMC 317 (dark grey). The resulting stitch is neither black nor grey but a visual blend that reads darker than grey and lighter than black.
Separate the skeins and cut one strand from each colour. Both strands should be the same length to avoid uneven wear.
Thread both strands through the needle eye together. The needle is now carrying a blend.

Stitch a sample fill on spare fabric and hold it at arm's length next to your pure black fill and your pure grey fill. Adjust the ratio if needed (two black, one grey, or one black, two grey) to reach the tone you want.
Using blending in a shaded piece

Blending can extend a limited fill vocabulary. If you only have three fill patterns but want five tonal values, use pure black for the darkest, a 2:0 black-to-grey blend for the second, a 1:1 blend for the third, a 0:2 grey-only fill for the fourth, and the most open fill pattern for the lightest area. Five tones from two thread colours and three fill designs.
